article_content: The family of jailed Australian journalist Peter Greste has apologized for a 'poorly worded' post on Twitter that led to speculation he would be deported. On Tuesday, his family tweeted that 'the Presidential Decree has been invoked' referring to a new Egyptian law allowing President Abdel Fattah al-Sissi to deport foreigners who have been sentenced to prison or are awaiting trial. Followers of the Al-Jazeera journalist quickly speculated about the tweet's meaning, with some even congratulating Greste on a possible deportation. Peter Greste, Canadian-Egyptian Mohammed Fahmy, and Egyptian Baher Mohammed were convicted in June 2014 of aiding the banned Muslim Brotherhood. The tweet from Greste's family stated: 'The Presidential Decree has been invoked. We are now waiting for respective governments to meet, discuss and negotiate possible deportation.' On Wednesday morning, Greste's family clarified and apologized for the post, explaining it was misinterpreted and that all paperwork has been submitted in hopes negotiations for deportation can begin. They apologized for any confusion, reiterating they are waiting for discussions to start. The tweet referenced the new law granting President al-Sissi authority to deport imprisoned or accused foreigners. Peter Greste's parents, Juris and Lois, continue to hope for their son's release from the Cairo prison where he has been held for over a year. Last week, a Cairo court ordered a retrial for Greste and his two Al-Jazeera colleagues following their conviction for aiding the banned Muslim Brotherhood. Greste, Fahmy, and Mohammed have been incarcerated for more than a year. Greste and Fahmy were sentenced to seven years, while Mohammed received ten years in June 2014. The families of Greste and Fahmy say they have applied to the government for deportation. In November, the Egyptian government introduced a decree allowing President al-Sissi to deport foreign defendants convicted or accused of crimes.

article_content: Betsy Duncan Smith, wife of former Work and Pensions Secretary Iain Duncan Smith, has spoken for the first time about her experience with breast cancer. Betsy, who has been married to Iain for 32 years and is a mother of four, said, 'My cancer was found very late. I didn’t notice any signs. Breast cancer took over my life for two years; the first part was the hardest. I couldn’t see a way out.' After her diagnosis, Betsy underwent six months of chemotherapy followed by radiotherapy. She shared, 'My energy levels dropped to zero. There were days I couldn’t walk or even talk. Iain had to bring his office home and look after me. It must have been very worrying for him, but he coped brilliantly.' Now 55, Betsy told the Daily Telegraph that losing her hair during treatment did not bother her: 'It was the least of my concerns. Eventually, I started to get stronger. I’ve recovered now, but I still have regular checkups.' Speaking with the Daily Mail about his wife’s diagnosis, Iain Duncan Smith, often called the 'quiet man' of politics, said: 'Betsy told me the doctor suspected it was cancer. He was right, and it took my breath away. I immediately went home and didn’t return to Parliament for some time.' Betsy now supports Medical Detection Dogs, a charity that trains dogs to detect illnesses in humans. She lives near the charity’s headquarters in Buckinghamshire and said, 'A friend invited me to visit the charity. At first, I was reluctant—I had just finished cancer treatment. But when I finally went, I was blown away.' Betsy has since adopted one of the charity’s cocker spaniels.

OpenAI, recognized for developing ChatGPT, made headlines by unexpectedly removing its co-founder and CEO, Sam Altman, last Friday. Altman, a leading advocate for artificial intelligence, was dismissed by the board, who cited concerns about his 'consistent candor' in communication. The abrupt nature of his departure has unsettled much of the technology sector.

Altman helped bring AI and products like ChatGPT into mainstream use, but the board has not provided detailed reasons for their lack of confidence. He had also been active in global discussions on AI safety, most recently attending an AI safety summit in the UK. According to reports, Altman had no prior warning of the move. Shortly after Altman’s exit, co-founder Greg Brockman was also dismissed from the board, a decision made by the remaining four of six board members.

There's ongoing speculation about why these changes occurred, though no evidence has surfaced of workplace misconduct or financial troubles—OpenAI was recently valued at approximately $80 billion. While Altman mentioned operational challenges due to growing demand for ChatGPT, it is unclear if this was a factor. 

Prominent figures in technology, such as Eric Schmidt and Satya Nadella, voiced support for Altman and OpenAI. Microsoft remains supportive as a major investor and has incorporated OpenAI’s technology into its services. On the other hand, Elon Musk, OpenAI’s co-founder, has withheld comment while his current company, X, released a competing chatbot called Grok. Some speculate that internal disputes over the company’s direction may have influenced the board’s decision.

For now, Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati, who previously worked at Tesla, is serving as interim CEO and will steer OpenAI through this period of uncertainty.

article_content: London (CNN) -- Amid uncertainty over his political future at home, Pakistani Prime Minister Yousuf Raza Gilani rejected U.S. claims that Pakistan was not doing enough in the fight against terrorism. Instead, he pointed to a trust deficit between Pakistan and the United States, stating in a CNN interview in London, "There's a trust deficit between both countries, between both governments. That is why we want to work towards new terms of engagement and cooperation with the United States." Pakistan has long been a key ally of the U.S., but relations have become increasingly strained, particularly after the killing of Osama bin Laden in Pakistan last year and a NATO airstrike in November that killed 24 Pakistani soldiers. Amidst the ongoing tensions, the Obama administration has expressed doubts that Pakistan was fully committed to fighting extremism. U.S. Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, at the end of an Asia tour on Tuesday, stated that Pakistan needs to do more in combating terrorism. In response, Gilani asserted that Pakistan was already working closely with the United States and urged Washington to share credible, actionable information. "If there is any credible, actionable information, please share it with us, because we are already working with you," he said. "My ISI is working with the CIA. What else do you want?" The ISI, Pakistan's powerful intelligence agency, has been accused by some U.S. officials of collaborating with militant groups. When asked how relations between the two countries could improve, Gilani replied, "One point: that is mutual respect and mutual interest." A lack of trust is only one aspect affecting this vital relationship. Pakistan continues to oppose U.S. drone strikes on its territory, a point Gilani reiterated on Tuesday. "We always consider drones counterproductive, and it's not lawful," he said. At home, Gilani faces multiple challenges, including a struggling economy, widespread poverty, corruption, and his own legal troubles. He was convicted last month of contempt of court for refusing to reopen old corruption cases against President Asif Ali Zardari. Some analysts predicted this conviction could plunge Pakistan into crisis and possibly trigger another military coup. Despite this, during a five-day visit to the United Kingdom, Gilani remained confident and defiant, insisting only parliament could remove him from office. "If I'm disqualified, and it is notified by the speaker, then yes, I have to step down," he said. On Tuesday, Pakistan's Supreme Court released a detailed verdict clarifying that Gilani was held in contempt for defying the country's highest judiciary. Gilani defended his actions, insisting everything he had done was constitutional and not related to moral or financial corruption. Gilani also said that Pakistan shares information about wanted terror suspects with the U.S. Regarding bin Laden, he claimed Pakistan was unaware of his residence in Abbottabad, calling it 'an intelligence failure of the whole world, not just of Pakistan.' He stressed that Pakistanis are well aware of the consequences of terrorism on their soil. Nevertheless, Clinton said the United States believes Ayman al-Zawahiri is hiding in Pakistan. Al-Zawahiri became al Qaeda's leader after bin Laden's death and is believed to have spent years hiding in Pakistan. Clinton highlighted the Rewards for Justice program, which offers up to $25 million for information on al-Zawahiri and up to $10 million for information about Hafiz Mohammad Saeed, who is wanted by Indian authorities for his alleged role in the 2008 Mumbai attacks that killed 166 people. When asked why Saeed remains free, Gilani said Pakistan is still 'waiting for credible information and evidence' that could be used in court. CNN's Jo Shelley contributed to this report.
translated_content: לונדון (CNN) -- בעיצומו של חוסר ודאות לגבי עתידו הפוליטי, ראש ממשלת פקיסטן יוסוף ראזה גילאני דחה את טענות ארה"ב כי פקיסטן לא עושה די במאבק בטרור. הוא הדגיש שקיים פער אמון בין פקיסטן לארצות הברית, ובראיון ל-CNN בלונדון אמר: "יש פער אמון בין שתי המדינות, בין שתי הממשלות. זו הסיבה שאנו רוצים לקדם תנאים חדשים של מעורבות ושיתוף פעולה עם ארצות הברית." פקיסטן הייתה בת ברית מרכזית של ארה"ב במשך שנים, אך היחסים הידרדרו במיוחד לאחר חיסול אוסאמה בן לאדן בפקיסטן בשנה שעברה ותקיפת נאט"ו בנובמבר, שבה נהרגו 24 חיילים פקיסטנים. על רקע המתיחות, ממשל אובמה הביע ספקות בנוגע למחויבות פקיסטן להיאבק בקיצוניות. מזכירת המדינה האמריקאית, הילרי קלינטון, אמרה בסוף ביקור באסיה שפקיסטן צריכה לעשות יותר במאבק בטרור. בתגובה, גילאני הדגיש כי פקיסטן כבר פועלת בשיתוף פעולה הדוק עם ארה"ב, וקרא לוושינגטון לשתף מידע מהימן ובר־ביצוע: "אם יש מידע מהימן ובר־ביצוע, שתפו אותנו, כי אנחנו כבר עובדים איתכם," אמר. "ה-ISI שלי עובד עם ה-CIA. מה עוד אתם רוצים?" סוכנות ה-ISI, סוכנות הביון של פקיסטן, הואשמה על ידי גורמים אמריקאים בקשרים עם קבוצות קיצוניות. על השאלה כיצד יחסים בין המדינות יכולים להשתפר, השיב: "נקודה אחת: כבוד הדדי ואינטרס הדדי." פער האמון הוא לא המכשול היחיד ביחסים. פקיסטן מתנגדת לתקיפות הכטב״מים (מל״טים) של ארה"ב בשטחה, וגילאני חזר על כך: "אנחנו תמיד רואים את התקיפות האלה כלא מועילות ולא חוקיות," אמר. בבית, גילאני מתמודד עם אתגרים כמו כלכלה מתדרדרת, עוני, שחיתות ובעיות משפטיות. הוא הורשע בחודש שעבר בביזיון בית המשפט – לאחר שסירב לפתוח מחדש תיקי שחיתות ישנים נגד הנשיא אסיף עלי זרדרי. יש אנליסטים שמעריכים כי הרשעה זו עלולה להביא את פקיסטן למשבר או אפילו לניסיון הפיכה צבאית. עם זאת, בביקור בן חמישה ימים בבריטניה נראה גילאני בטוח בעצמו ועמד על כך שרק הפרלמנט יכול להדיח אותו. "אם אני נפסל, והיו"ר יודיע לי, אז כן אאלץ להתפטר," אמר. ביום שלישי בית המשפט העליון של פקיסטן פרסם פסק-דין מפורט שמבהיר כי גילאני הורשע בביזיון בשל התעלמות מהפסיקה הגבוהה במדינה. גילאני טען כי כל מעשיו עולים בקנה אחד עם החוקה ואינם קשורים לפגם מוסרי או שחיתות כספית. הוא הדגיש כי פקיסטן משתפת מידע על מבוקשי טרור עם ארה"ב. לגבי בן לאדן, אמר כי פקיסטן לא ידעה על שהותו באבוטאבאד – 'זה היה כישלון מודיעיני עולמי, לא רק של פקיסטן'. לדבריו, הפקיסטנים מודעים מאוד להשלכות הטרור בארצם. למרות זאת, קלינטון טוענת שארה"ב מאמינה שאיימן אל-זוואהירי מסתתר בפקיסטן. אל-זוואהירי ירש את הנהגת אל-קאעידה לאחר מותו של בן לאדן ומעריכים ששהה במסתור בפקיסטן. קלינטון הדגישה את תוכנית "תגמול לצדק", שמציעה עד 25 מיליון דולר על מידע על אל-זוואהירי ועד 10 מיליון דולר על חאפיז מוחמד סעיד, החשוד בהובלת מתקפת מומבאי ב-2008 שבה נהרגו 166 אנשים. בנוגע לכך שסעיד עדיין חופשי, אמר גילאני כי פקיסטן "מחכה למידע ואישומים קונקרטיים וברורים" שניתן להציג בבית המשפט. ג'ו שלי מ-CNN תרמה לכתבה.

article_content: Raheem Sterling’s presence truly highlights the youthful nature of England’s World Cup squad. His first full memory of the tournament is from South Africa 2010, watching Steven Gerrard score while spending time with friends. Now, at only 19 years old, Sterling is training with the national team and looking forward to making his mark on football’s biggest stage. Just four years ago, Sterling was a 15-year-old playing on St Raphael’s Estate near Wembley Stadium. He was already on QPR’s books before joining Liverpool at 16. Although Luke Shaw is the youngest in the squad, Sterling is widely seen as the young player most likely to make a big impact. Recently, Sterling played a crucial role in Liverpool’s push for the league title, transforming from a backup into a key contributor thanks to his pace and skill. His performances, particularly against teams like Arsenal, stood out. He remembers the excitement of playing for Liverpool and the thrill of the fans’ support during the final matches. England has a history of promoting young talents like Theo Walcott, Michael Owen, and Wayne Rooney. Sterling hopes his World Cup experience will be more similar to Owen’s, who shone as a teenager, rather than Walcott’s, who didn’t play. He is focused on working hard and giving his best, resisting pressure to predict outstanding achievements. Sterling mentions he was initially nervous joining the England squad but found comfort through the support of his Liverpool teammates. Originally from Jamaica, he moved to London when he was five and earned his first England cap at 17, making him one of the youngest debutants. Sterling faced challenges, including being left out of the first team by manager Brendan Rodgers and dealing with rumors about his personal life. Nevertheless, he made a comeback, contributing to Liverpool’s success and showing he could play various attacking positions. Although praised by Rodgers as one of Europe’s top young players, Sterling stays humble and gives credit to his mother for helping him stay grounded. He is ready to embrace whatever comes next in his career.

article_content: Mark Howell, a councillor at South Cambridgeshire District Council responsible for housing policy, has issued an apology after an email he sent six years ago containing offensive language towards travellers resurfaced. The email included an image of a mocked-up road sign with derogatory text and was circulated among fellow councillors when Howell was part of an independent group. Details of the email have only recently emerged after it was leaked by political opponents. Howell is now a Conservative and continues to play a key role in the district's housing and traveller site policies. Opposition councillors, including Robin Page, have called for Howell's resignation from the cabinet and the council, describing his actions as intolerable and disgraceful. Howell acknowledged the email was inappropriate and apologized for any offense caused, stating that it was intended as a private joke within the independent group and does not reflect his views. The incident has gained attention as Howell supports plans to reopen the controversial Mettle Hill traveller site in Meldreth, Cambridgeshire, a project costing the authority an estimated £500,000 and aiming to provide 20 additional pitches by 2031 to meet legal obligations. The project has been opposed by South Cambridgeshire MP and Leader of the House of Commons, Andrew Lansley. Some opponents also accuse Howell of overlooking other potential sites for travellers.

article_content: A senior United Nations official has cautioned that, if there is no progress in resolving the Syrian conflict, the number of people fleeing Syria as refugees could increase two or threefold by the end of the year. More than a million Syrians have already left their country since the civil war began two years ago. Antonio Guterres, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, stated in Ankara, Turkey, that the number of Syrians leaving the country rose dramatically—from 3,000 per day in December to 8,000 per day by February. Guterres indicated that if the current conditions persist, 'the refugee numbers might double or triple by year’s end.' The UN’s earlier estimate anticipated that 1.1 million Syrians would relocate to nearby countries by June, but this figure will be exceeded this month. The majority are seeking safety in neighboring countries such as Lebanon, Jordan, Turkey, Iraq, and Egypt, though a growing number are making their way to North Africa and Europe. The arrival of so many refugees is placing immense pressure on regional infrastructure and resources. The UNHCR has noted that Jordan’s energy, healthcare, and education systems are severely strained, and Turkey has invested $600 million in 17 refugee camps. Many Syrians avoid registering as refugees due to concerns about potential consequences if they return home or because they are hesitant to accept outside assistance. Jordanian military personnel shared with CNN their efforts to support incoming Syrians, though they admitted they are overwhelmed by the sheer numbers. Some rebel fighters, who have brought their families to camps in Jordan, informed CNN correspondent Nick Paton Walsh that they intend to return to Syria — especially to Daraa — to continue fighting. Others have observed that many families are leaving and few people remain in their neighborhoods, with one boy saying, 'You can now count the people left on your fingers. Syria is emptying.' The crisis started in March 2011 when President Bashar al-Assad’s government responded to calls for political reform with harsh crackdowns. The unrest has escalated into an armed conflict, causing extensive destruction across the country.

article_content: Hundreds of well-wishers attended the funeral of 94-year-old Frederick Leach, a Second World War veteran who passed away without any close family. Leach, who had survived numerous life-threatening situations during the war, was recognized for his involvement in the Liberation of Norway. Leach died on November 6, 2013, at Briarwood Care Home in Eston, Middlesbrough. After an appeal by Redcar and Cleveland Council, around 300 people gathered at Teesside Crematorium to pay their respects to the veteran. The 45-minute ceremony was led by Jon Edwards, minister of South Bank Baptist Church, where Leach once attended. Both members of the Armed Forces, veterans, and members of the public were present. Edwards described Leach as a dignified and proud man, dedicated to his military service and integrity. Leach served as a private in B Company of the 1st Battalion of the Green Howards during the 1940 Norway campaign. Despite facing overwhelming odds and attacks by Stuka dive bombers, his battalion held their line. Leach survived this and was one of the last members remaining from that battle years later. Among attendees were Earnie Jackson, a fellow veteran, and Dennis Grubb, a standard bearer from the Royal Air Force Association, who praised the turnout of approximately 300 people, including about 100 who listened outside the chapel. Sheelagh Clarke, from Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council, called the public and Armed Forces community response 'truly heart-warming.' A similar tribute was paid to Harold Jellicoe Percival, another veteran who died with few known family. After his story was shared, hundreds attended his funeral as well. Leach was later honored at the 60th anniversary of Norway’s liberation, where he met King Harald of Norway and the Duke of Edinburgh, proudly wearing his Green Howards blazer.

article_content: Same-sex marriage is a step closer to becoming legal in North Carolina, with a federal lawsuit challenging the state's ban. Ellen 'Lennie' Gerber and Pearl Berlin of High Point, a couple together for 48 years, are the lead plaintiffs. Berlin, age 89 and in fragile health, has been hospitalized multiple times recently, adding urgency to their fight. Though legally married in Maine in 2013, their marriage remains unrecognized in North Carolina due to a voter-approved constitutional amendment. The couple's litigation seeks immediate recognition of their marriage. Their relationship began on June 2, 1966, a date inscribed in Roman numerals on matching gold rings exchanged during a religious ceremony at their Greensboro synagogue. Both have backgrounds in education and are longtime advocates for civil rights. Recent federal court decisions have overturned same-sex marriage bans in other states within the 4th Circuit, igniting optimism that North Carolina may soon follow. State Attorney General Roy Cooper has stated it would be 'futile' to defend the ban further, although some state leaders want to continue fighting the legal challenge. Gerber and Berlin worry about access to spousal rights during medical emergencies, fearing that despite legal power-of-attorney documents, hospital staff may not recognize their relationship. The couple hope for a judicial ruling that grants immediate recognition to same-sex marriages in North Carolina, emphasizing the profound personal and legal impact. Their home is filled with memories from a life built together: art, travel mementos, and photos from every continent. Family acceptance came gradually, but the two have lived openly as a couple since the 1960s, despite social stigmas and barriers in professional life. Gerber, now a retired lawyer, has dedicated her career to helping other LGBTQ couples navigate legal protections. However, she notes no document matches the security of a marriage certificate for ensuring spousal rights. Looking toward their 50th anniversary, the couple hope the law will finally recognize the relationship they have celebrated for nearly half a century.

article_content: Three key witnesses in the case of Rimsha Masih, a 14-year-old Christian girl in Pakistan accused of blasphemy, have retracted their earlier statements. Rimsha was charged over a month ago under Pakistan’s blasphemy laws for allegedly burning pages of the Quran for cooking fuel, a charge she denies. Initially, the witnesses told police they saw Khalid Jadoon Chishti, a local Muslim cleric, tear pages from a Quran and add them to the evidence used against Rimsha. However, at Chishti’s bail hearing, the three changed their testimonies, according to Chishti’s lawyer, Wajid Ali Gilani. A fourth witness maintained his original account. The witnesses’ testimony plays a crucial role in the police investigation, which recently concluded that Rimsha was framed. Based on these findings and the lack of reliable witnesses, Rimsha’s lawyers are seeking for the charges to be dropped. The case has sparked widespread international concern, with critics arguing that Pakistan’s blasphemy laws are often used to persecute religious minorities or settle personal disputes. Islamabad’s police chief, Bin Yamin, has accused the three witnesses of perjury and insisted there was no coercion when they gave their initial statements. "If they have changed their statements, they are just lying," he told reporters. Rimsha was arrested in August after a neighbor accused her of burning Quranic pages, which led to public outrage in her community. Reports say some neighbors beat her, while others claim she ran home and locked herself inside. After her arrest, she was detained in an adult jail until she was released on bail in September. Rimsha’s lawyers allege the neighbor’s accusation was motivated by a personal grudge, citing their strained relationship. They contend that no one witnessed Rimsha burning the pages; rather, the neighbor delivered the evidence to Chishti. According to police, Chishti was unsure whether burnt pages would suffice for conviction, so he allegedly added two pages from a Quran to strengthen the case. Chishti may now face charges for tampering with evidence and possibly blasphemy. Human Rights Watch’s Pakistan director, Ali Dayan Hasan, noted that pursuing false accuser charges is unprecedented in the 25-year history of Pakistan’s blasphemy laws. Last week, a local court transferred Rimsha’s case to juvenile court following the police findings. The Islamabad High Court is scheduled to hear her petition for dismissing the charges on October 17, said her lawyer, Abdul Hamid Rana. If not dismissed, the case will continue in juvenile court. Hasan of Human Rights Watch described the transfer as a promising sign towards ending the case, noting how rare such action is under Pakistan's blasphemy laws. The current impact of the witness retractions on Rimsha’s case remains undetermined. Since the enactment of the blasphemy laws in 1986, Human Rights Watch reports there have been 1,400 blasphemy cases, with over 15 people currently on death row and 52 killed during trial in Pakistan. After her release, Rimsha expressed relief to be with her family but also shared fears for their safety, stating, "I'm scared. I'm afraid of anyone who might kill us." Although aid organizations in the US, Italy, and Canada have offered refuge, Rimsha has indicated she wishes to remain in Pakistan.
translated_content: שלושה עדים מרכזיים בפרשת רימשה מסיח, נערה נוצרית בת 14 מפקיסטן המואשמת בבעילת דת, חזרו בהם מהצהרותיהם המוקדמות. רימשה הואשמה לפני יותר מחודש על פי חוקי הבעילת דת של פקיסטן בכך ששרפה דפים מהקוראן לשימוש כדלק לבישול, אך היא מכחישה את האישום. בהתחלה העדים אמרו למשטרה כי ראו את ח'אליד ג'דון צ'ישטי, איש דת מוסלמי מקומי, קורע דפים מהקוראן ומוסיף אותם לראיות נגד רימשה. אולם, בדיון בערבות של צ'ישטי, שלושת העדים שינו את עדותם, כך לדברי עורך דינו של צ'ישטי, ואג'יד עלי גילאני. עד רביעי התמיד בגרסתו המקורית. עדות העדים מהווה גורם מכריע בחקירת המשטרה, שהגיעה למסקנה לאחרונה שרימשה הופללה. על בסיס מסקנות אלה והיעדר עדים מהימנים, עורכי דינה של רימשה מבקשים לבטל את האישומים נגדה. הפרשה עוררה דאגה בינלאומית נרחבת, כאשר מבקרים טוענים כי חוקי הבעילת דת של פקיסטן משמשים לעתים ככלי לרדיפת מיעוטים דתיים או לסגירת חשבונות אישיים. מפקד משטרת אסלאמאבאד, בין יאמין, האשים את שלושת העדים בשבועת שקר והתעקש שלא הופעל לחץ כשהעדים מסרו את הצהרותיהם הראשונות. "אם הם שינו את עדותם, הם פשוט משקרים", אמר לעיתונאים. רימשה נעצרה באוגוסט לאחר ששכן האשים אותה בשריפת דפי קוראן, מה שגרם לזעם ציבורי בקהילתה. לפי הדיווחים, כמה שכנים היכו אותה, ואחרים סיפרו שהיא ברחה לביתה ונעלה את עצמה בפנים. לאחר מעצרה, היא הוחזקה בבית סוהר למבוגרים עד ששוחררה בערבות בספטמבר. עורכי דינה של רימשה טוענים כי האישום של השכן נבע מסכסוך אישי, תוך ציון מערכת יחסים מתוחה ביניהם. לטענתם, אף אחד לא ראה את רימשה שורפת את הדפים, והשכן הוא זה שהעביר את הראיות לצ'ישטי. לדברי המשטרה, צ'ישטי לא היה בטוח שדפים שרופים יספיקו להרשעה, ולכן לכאורה הוסיף שני דפים מקוראן כדי לחזק את התיק. כעת ייתכן שיינתנו נגדו כתבי אישום על שיבוש ראיות ואולי אף על בעילת דת. מנהל Human Rights Watch בפקיסטן, עלי דיאן חסן, הדגיש כי הגשת כתבי אישום נגד מאשימים שקריים היא צעד נדיר מאוד בהיסטוריה של חוקי הבעילת דת בפקיסטן. בשבוע שעבר בית משפט מקומי העביר את התיק של רימשה לבית המשפט לנוער בעקבות ממצאי המשטרה. בית המשפט הגבוה לאסלאמאבאד צפוי לדון בבקשה לביטול האישומים ב-17 באוקטובר, לדברי עורך דינה עבדול חמיד רנה. אם הבקשה תדחה, הדיונים יימשכו בבית המשפט לנוער. חסן מ-Human Rights Watch תיאר את המהלך כהתקדמות חיובית לסיום הפרשה, וציין עד כמה הוא נדיר במסגרת החוק. השפעות שינויי העדויות על עתידה של רימשה עדיין לא ידועות. מאז חקיקת חוקי הבעילת דת בשנת 1986, Human Rights Watch דיווח על 1,400 מקרים, למעלה מ-15 אנשים ממתינים להוצאה להורג ו-52 נהרגו במהלך משפטם בפקיסטן. לאחר שחרור, רימשה סיפרה שהיא שמחה להיות שוב עם משפחתה אך מודאגת לבטיחותם: "אני מפחדת. אני חוששת שמישהו יהרוג אותנו." למרות שארגוני סיוע מארה"ב, איטליה וקנדה הציעו לה מקלט, רימשה ציינה שהיא רוצה להישאר בפקיסטן.

Once famous for its ancient heritage and vibrant daily life, Homs in central Syria is now at the heart of the nation’s most violent fighting. For almost a year, President Bashar al-Assad’s government forces have pounded the city to push back against anti-government protests. Activists estimate that since January, hundreds have died from relentless shelling and sniper attacks as the regime tries to regain control of the city, long considered a symbol of the uprising.

Homs is suffering a rapidly worsening humanitarian emergency: casualties rise each day, and hospitals cannot keep up with the needs of the injured due to limited staff and scarce medical supplies. Makeshift field hospitals often operate out of private homes, and many wounded people do not receive treatment in time to save their lives.

Strategically, Homs is vital. Its location connects Syria’s capital, Damascus, with the northern city of Aleppo, and a major oil refinery in the city is critical for government operations. The population, noted for its diversity—mainly Sunni Muslims, but also significant numbers of Alawite Muslims and Christians—makes the situation more complicated as tensions rise.

Historically, Homs’s communities coexisted closely. Chris Phillips, an analyst specializing in Syria, notes that while residents have been subjects of national jokes, they contribute significantly to the country’s culture and education. Now, however, violence and the presence of pro-government militias (the shabiha) are deepening divides between the established Sunni community and newer Alawite migrants.

Safety is fragile across Homs, with widespread power cuts and regular raids where authorities sever communications in opposition-held areas. People face shortages of essential items like fuel and baby formula, and access to aid is often blocked. Snipers endanger anyone on the streets, and ambulances aren’t safe either.

Activist Abu Rami, who uses an alias for security, shared that he hid for days at a friend’s house, terrified of arrest or death. Rami had left his university studies in medicine to support anti-regime protests. The city’s normal rhythm is disrupted, with shops closing early and streets empty as families try to stay safe.

Homs is now heavily militarized—dozens of checkpoints and tanks surround the city. Many residents fear a tragedy similar to the 1982 Hama massacre, where thousands were killed in a regime crackdown. President Assad, in a television interview, distanced himself from direct responsibility for the army, insisting they are government forces, not his own.

Amid the ongoing violence, old community bonds are fraying. Phillips explains that some Sunnis resent new Alawite arrivals, while Alawites worry about reprisals if the regime falls. The regime, Phillips believes, exploits these fears to hold onto support from minorities.

Despite everything, hope persists in Homs. Rami dreams of rebuilding his life there if peace returns. He sums up the city’s grim stakes: “Either we all die, or we win in the end.”

העיר חומס שבמרכז סוריה, שפעם הייתה ידועה במורשתה ובחיים התוססים, הפכה לזירה המרכזית של הקרבות האכזריים במדינה. קרוב לשנה שכוחות נשיא סוריה בשאר אל-אסד מפעילים אש כבדה על העיר בניסיון לדכא את ההתקוממות. פעילים מדווחים שמאז ינואר נהרגו מאות תושבים מהפצצות וירי צלפים, כשכוחות המשטר מנסים להשיב שליטה על חומס – העיר השלישית בגודלה במדינה וסמל ההתנגדות.

המשבר ההומניטרי בחומס מחמיר: מספר ההרוגים גדל מדי יום, ובתי החולים מתקשים לעמוד בעומס בשל מחסור חמור בצוות רפואי וציוד. קליניקות שדה רבות מוקמות בבתי מגורים, והרבה פצועים אינם זוכים לטיפול מתאים בזמן.

חומס בעלת חשיבות אסטרטגית – מיקומה מחבר את דמשק ואלפו, ובתחומה נמצא אחד מבתי הזיקוק העיקריים במדינה, דבר קריטי להמשך שליטת המשטר. הרכב האוכלוסייה בעיר מגוון: רוב סוני, מיעוט עלאווי ומספר נוצרים – מציאות שמסבכת עוד יותר את המצב.

לפני הסכסוך, תושבי חומס חיו יחדיו, למרות סטיגמות שנקשרו להם. עם התגברות האלימות ומעורבותם של אנשי שביחה – מיליציות פרו-משטר – הקרע בין הקהילה הסונית והעלאווית העמיק.

כיום חיי היום-יום קשים: בחלקים נרחבים אין חשמל, המשטר מנתק תקשורת לפני פשיטות, יש מחסור חריף במזון, דלק וחלב לתינוקות, וגישה לטיפול רפואי מוגבלת מאוד. צלפים מסכנים את העוברים והשבים, וגם אמבולנסים לא מוגנים.

אבו ראמי, פעיל המשתמש בשם בדוי, מספר שהסתתר ימים אצל חבר כי חשש לחייו. הוא עזב את לימודי הרפואה כדי לעזור למפגינים, וכעת חומס מושבתת – החנויות נסגרות מוקדם, הרחובות ריקים.

מספר המחסומים הרב, נוכחות טנקים, והזיכרונות מהטבח בחמא ב-1982 גורמים לחשש מהסלמה דומה. אסד, בראיון טלוויזיוני, הדגיש כי כוחות הצבא אינם בבעלותו אלא שייכים למדינה.

הסכסוך משנה את יחסי הקהילות בחומס: מתחים גוברים בין הסונים לעלאווים והמשטר מנצל את החששות. למרות הכל, רבים מתושבי העיר עדיין חולמים על עתיד טוב יותר; ראמי אומר: "או שכולנו נמות – או שננצח בסוף."

article_content: The Indian government has implemented a standard operating procedure (SOP) to streamline and accelerate the visa approval process for Chinese professionals whose expertise is needed by vendors under the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, an official stated on Wednesday. Visa approval challenges had been raised in a stakeholder meeting regarding the PLI scheme in August, prompting the government to create a dedicated system to resolve these issues, ensuring smoother entry for the required professionals. Introduced in 2021, the PLI scheme covers 14 sectors—including telecommunications, white goods, textiles, medical devices manufacturing, automobiles, specialty steel, food products, high-efficiency solar PV modules, advanced chemistry cell batteries, drones, and pharmaceuticals—and is backed by a total allocation of Rs 1.97 lakh crore. Separately, India's fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) sector experienced a 9% rise in value sales and an 8.6% increase in volume for the September quarter, driven largely by increased rural demand, according to NielsenIQ. In the technology domain, Snapchat's parent company, Snap Inc., saw its user base in India double to 200 million over the past year, credited to the success of products like Spotlight. Additionally, the finance ministry is considering slowing the pace of capital expenditure increases in the upcoming interim budget for FY25 to better align with fiscal consolidation objectives.
translated_content: ממשלת הודו יישמה נוהל עבודה סטנדרטי (SOP) לצורך ייעול ולהאצת תהליך אישור הוויזות לאנשי מקצוע מסין שנדרשים לספקים במסגרת תוכנית התמרוץ לייצור (PLI), כך נמסר ביום רביעי. סוגיית הוויזות עלתה לפתחו של הממשל בפגישת שיתוף פעולה עם בעלי עניין באוגוסט, ובעקבות זאת גיבשה הממשלה מערכת ייעודית לפתרון ולשיפור תהליך הכניסה של אותם מומחים נחוצים. תוכנית PLI, שהושקה ב-2021, כוללת 14 תחומים — בהם טלקום, מוצרי חשמל ביתיים, טקסטיל, ייצור מכשור רפואי, רכב, פלדה ייחודית, מוצרי מזון, מודולים סולאריים, סוללות כימיה מתקדמת, רחפנים ותרופות — עם תקציב כולל של 1.97 לאך קרור רופי. במקביל, מגזר מוצרי הצריכה המהירים (FMCG) בהודו רשם עלייה של 9% במכירות ובהיקף של 8.6% ברבעון ספטמבר, בעיקר בזכות ביקוש גובר באזורים הכפריים, כך לפי נתוני NielsenIQ. בתחום הטכנולוגיה, חברת Snap Inc., הבעלים של Snapchat, הכפילה את מספר המשתמשים בהודו ל-200 מיליון בשנה האחרונה בעיקר בזכות פיצ'ר Spotlight. בנוסף, משרד האוצר שוקל להאט את קצב גידול ההוצאה ההונית בתקציב המעבר לשנת 2025, במטרה לעמוד ביעדי ההתייעלות הפיסקלית.

Grigor Dimitrov demonstrated impressive determination to defeat Kevin Anderson in a hard-fought three-hour ATP final in Acapulco, Mexico. The 22-year-old Bulgarian secured the win 7-6, 3-6, 7-6, completing the match shortly after 1 a.m. local time. Dimitrov didn’t waste his first match point, prompting his girlfriend Maria Sharapova to tweet that his performance was inspiring. Only one service break occurred throughout the close match on Acapulco's fast hard courts.

With Roger Rasheed as his coach, Dimitrov is expected to climb to 16th in the world rankings, after a notable semifinal victory over Andy Murray that had left him physically exhausted. Reflecting on the challenge, Dimitrov told the ATP Tour website, "Belief is the only thing that kept me going today... This title means a lot to me. Every match, especially the last three, went to three sets."

Dimitrov comfortably claimed the first-set tiebreak 7-1, but Anderson answered with a break in the second set, leading to a final set showdown. At 5-5 in the third, Anderson's backhand sailed long, giving Dimitrov a chance to close out the match, which he seized immediately. This is Dimitrov's second ATP title. His style, likened to Roger Federer’s, has earned him the nickname ‘Baby Federer,’ and he may soon join a management group co-founded by Federer and agent Roger Godsick.

Federer himself clinched his sixth Dubai title over Tomas Berdych this weekend. Both Federer and Dimitrov now head to Indian Wells for the Masters 1000 tournament, with Dimitrov considered a strong outsider following his recent form.

On the women’s side in Acapulco, Dominika Cibulkova defeated Christina McHale 7-6, 4-6, 6-4 to capture her fourth career title, following her recent runner-up finish at the Australian Open to Li Na.

גריגור דימיטרוב גילה נחישות מרשימה כשניצח את קווין אנדרסון בגמר ATP מתוח שנמשך שלוש שעות באקפולקו, מקסיקו. הבולגרי בן ה-22 ניצח 7-6, 3-6, 7-6, וסיים את המשחק מעט אחרי אחת בלילה (זמן מקומי). דימיטרוב ניצל את נקודת המשחק הראשונה שלו, מה שגרם לחברתו מריה שרפובה לצייץ שזו הייתה הופעה מעוררת השראה. במשחק הצמוד נשבר רק משחקון אחד על המשטחים הקשים המהירים של אקפולקו.

בהדרכת המאמן רוג'ר ראשיד, דימיטרוב צפוי לעלות למקום ה-16 בעולם, אחרי ניצחון חצי גמר משמעותי על אנדי מארי, שהשאיר אותו מותש פיזית. דימיטרוב סיפר לאתר ATP: "האמונה היא שהחזיקה אותי היום... התואר הזה חשוב לי מאוד. כל המשחקים, ובעיקר שלושת האחרונים, היו קשים ונגררו לשלוש מערכות".

דימיטרוב זכה בטיי-ברייק ראשון 7-1, אבל אנדרסון הגיב בשבירה במערכה השנייה וכפה הכרעה. ב-5-5 במערכה השלישית, חבטת גב יד של אנדרסון יצאה החוצה ודימיטרוב מיד ניצל את ההזדמנות וסגר את הניצחון. זהו התואר השני של דימיטרוב ב-ATP. סגנון המשחק שלו גרם לו להיקרא 'בייבי פדרר', וייתכן שיצטרף בקרוב לקבוצת הניהול החדשה של רוג'ר פדרר והסוכן שלו, רוג'ר גודסיק.

פדרר עצמו זכה בתואר השישי שלו בדובאי אחרי ניצחון על תומאש ברדיך. השניים מתכוננים לטורניר מאסטרס 1000 באינדיאן וולס, שם דימיטרוב מגיע בכושר מצוין.

article_content: Today, using social media is a big part of finding and keeping a job. Sites like Twitter and Facebook make networking and building your personal brand easier, but they've also led to some regrettable mistakes—including firings. Take the example of a soon-to-be Cisco employee who tweeted, 'Cisco just offered me a job! Now I have to weigh the utility of a fatty paycheck against the daily commute to San Jose and hating the work.' Someone at Cisco saw the post, which led to awkward questions about his attitude. Plenty of others have been tripped up online. Web marketer Paul Wilson tracked down numerous tweets from people complaining about their jobs, bosses, and coworkers—sometimes even confessing to questionable actions at work. These posts, though often impulsive, can backfire if noticed by employers. Issues aren't limited to Twitter. In the UK, Kimberly Swann was dismissed after posting about her boring job on Facebook. Kevin Colvin, an intern, said he had a family emergency but was discovered at a Halloween party thanks to Facebook photos. In another case, Dan Leone lost his job with the Philadelphia Eagles after criticizing a player trade on his Facebook status. The takeaway is clear: posts you make online can come back to haunt you, especially when employers are watching. If you want to use social media to your advantage, or at least avoid harming your career, follow these guidelines: 1. Don’t post details about interviews, pay raises, or new job offers if you’re currently employed. Sharing such news in vague terms is fine, but be careful with specifics. 2. Steer clear of badmouthing your company, colleagues, or boss online. It damages your professional reputation and can lead to job loss. 3. Avoid disclosing your job search publicly if your current employer isn’t aware. Even if you think your boss isn’t online, information spreads easily. Always think carefully about how your online presence reflects on your career!

article_content: Just as Marvel Comics has imprints for alternate universe stories, DC Comics offered Elseworlds. This line was discontinued after 2010, succeeded by imprints like Earth One (which was also short-lived), Black Label, and young adult graphic novels. Many now know 'Elseworlds' from the Arrowverse crossover in 2018. At New York Comic-Con, DC announced Elseworlds is returning in 2024. The first six books will include new stories such as Green Lantern Dark by Tate Brombal and Werther Dell’Edera, and Batman the Barbarian by Greg Smallwood, which places Batman in a medieval setting. Recent alternate universe stories—Dark Knights of Steel: Allwinter by Jay Kristoff and Tirso Cons, and DC vs. Vampires: World War V by Matthew Rosenberg and Otto Schmidt—will also join the imprint. DC Executive Editor Ben Abernathy stated, 'Out-of-continuity stories have always been a pillar of DC publishing, granting creators the ability to explore all the wild corners of the DC Universe.' He added that they are excited to relaunch ELSEWORLDS in 2024, featuring both new works and sequels that fit the out-of-continuity approach. Elseworlds started in 1991 with Batman: Holy Terror by Alan Brennert and Norm Breyfogle. Celebrated stories under this label—like Superman: Red Son (Mark Millar) and Kingdom Come (Mark Waid, Alex Ross)—have become favorites among fans and have shaped the DC brand. Now, Elseworlds also names DC movies and shows outside the main continuity managed by James Gunn and Peter Safran, such as The Batman, the Harley Quinn cartoon, and Todd Phillips’ Joker films. Given DC’s tendency to adapt various stories for direct-to-video releases, it’s likely some new Elseworlds tales may receive animated adaptations in coming years. More information on Elseworlds titles releasing in 2024 is available online. For further pop culture coverage, check announcements for Marvel, Star Wars, Star Trek releases, latest DC film and TV news, and future updates on Doctor Who.

CNN's Art of Life presents a special episode featuring renowned fashion designer Tom Ford, granting viewers an inside look at his personal and creative worlds. Host Monita Rajpal meets Ford in Milan for the launch of his new men's fragrance, travels to his flagship Tom Ford menswear store on Madison Avenue in New York, and joins him as he explores favorite spots in London.

Ford revisits his transformative influence on luxury fashion through his work at Gucci and Yves Saint Laurent in the 1990s. With his current brand, Tom Ford Menswear, he continues to champion elegance and aims to redefine modern luxury. While in Milan, Ford shares his reasons for forgoing traditional runway presentations and outlines his plans for the brand from New York.

Though widely recognized as a showman, Ford reveals his more private nature, discussing personal experiences that have shaped his career. The program also highlights Ford's affection for London, one of several cities where he resides—including Los Angeles, Santa Fe, Austin, and London. Rajpal is given a tour of Ford's London home, enjoys a meal at Scott's in Mayfair, and visits the White Cube gallery—places that embody Ford's pursuit of culture and relaxation.

article_content: The Dozy Mmobuosi Foundation, a non-governmental organization focused on cancer awareness and management, hosted a 3.3km walk in Lagos on Saturday to promote awareness about prostate cancer. The event, which started from Ikeja Under Bridge and ended at Ikeja City Mall in Alausa, Ikeja, was called 'The Dozy Mmobuosi Foundation March For Men Against Prostate Cancer.' During the walk, free prostate cancer screenings were provided to men aged 45 and above, along with blood pressure and blood sugar checks. Prostate cancer affects the prostate gland and, according to medical experts, is highly treatable if detected early. It is currently the most common cancer among men. According to the World Health Organisation, Nigeria recorded approximately 115,950 prostate cancer cases and 70,327 related deaths in 2018. The disease is recognized globally as a significant health challenge for men, especially when not caught early. At the event, Dr. Adebowale Oyebade, Senior Registrar Urologist at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, encouraged men over 40 to undergo annual prostate screenings to prevent late detection, which limits treatment options. He noted that late diagnosis makes prostate cancer harder to treat and increases death risk. Dr. Oyebade stressed the wide-reaching impact of prostate cancer, highlighting that it not only affects men but also their families. He described it as a major public health issue in Nigeria and across Africa. He explained, 'Prostate cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death among men. About one in eight men will develop prostate issues in their lifetime, and one in 38 will die from prostate cancer.' He emphasized that regular screenings and early detection can improve treatment outcomes and reduce financial burdens on families. Toyin Ayodele, Head of Business Development at the Dozy Mmobuosi Foundation, spoke on the importance of yearly testing for men over 40, stressing that early detection can lead to a cure. She stated, 'Our goal is to increase awareness about prostate cancer among Nigerian men and encourage them to get tested. The walk was organized to offer free screenings and help people know their health status.' The event also saw participation from top celebrities in Nigeria’s Nollywood and music industry, helping to draw attention to the cause and encourage more men to get screened.

Caroline Wozniacki has criticized the underwear checks conducted by Wimbledon officials, describing them as 'creepy.' The former fiancée of Rory McIlroy voiced her concerns after several players expressed that the strict enforcement of the tournament’s all-white dress code could compromise their dignity. Due to the increased scrutiny, some players have chosen to forgo wearing bras, while others noted that wearing white underwear beneath a white dress can appear see-through when sweating.

Wozniacki stated she wears white underwear at Wimbledon but added, 'I don't think anyone is showing off their underwear, but getting it checked would be pretty creepy.' This year, the All England Club introduced stricter dress code guidelines in response to concerns that sponsors were incorporating colored elements in players’ clothing. The updated regulations mandate that every item, including undergarments, must be completely white, leaving little room for interpretation.

Czech player Barbora Zahlavova Strycova said, 'We’re playing in white so we should wear white underwear, but it’s weird for officials to check. I think it’s strange.' Former champion Pat Cash mentioned that some female players had been ordered to change bras and tops due to slight color, and lacking suitable replacements, had to play without proper support. Swiss player Belinda Bencic, who won her second-round match on the same day, supported the dress code, stating, 'I have always tried to wear white underpants. White at Wimbledon is a nice tradition, so I think it is really nice to do that.'

Virgin Atlantic founder Richard Branson praised the pilots and team on Twitter for their safe and skillful landing, and expressed support for passengers and crew. CEO Craig Kreeger acknowledged the disruption to holiday plans and promised that all passengers would be cared for, offering a special flight the following day for those continuing their journey.

After his wife Liz couldn’t join their family on camping trips due to the limitations of traditional wheelchairs, Brad Soden of Phoenix built the first 'Tankchair': a wheelchair equipped with caterpillar tracks for tackling rough, outdoor terrain. Although he lacked formal engineering training, Brad’s hands-on experience with tracked vehicles during his military service helped guide his do-it-yourself approach as he developed and improved prototypes from his garage.

Witnessing the emotional impact on his wife and family motivated Brad to create a solution, eventually enlisting Arizona-based NPC Robotics to help refine the Tankchair. Priced around $15,000, each chair is built to order and can be customized with features like fishing rod holders, text-to-speech systems, or specialized LED lights for law enforcement clients.

Brad’s Tankchairs have made a significant difference for wounded veterans, with the support of the NFL and encouragement from public figures like Bill O’Reilly and Eddie Vedder. Pixar even sought Brad’s advice during the creation of the animated film Wall-E to lend authenticity to their wheelchair designs.

Continuing his mission, Brad is now testing an advanced model dubbed the 'Speedster,' which can reach speeds of up to 30 mph. Through his innovations, he aims to change perceptions and expand possibilities for wheelchair users everywhere.

article_content: A recently uncovered diary has revealed that the frozen body of legendary explorer George Mallory was spotted on Everest decades before it was officially discovered. Frank Smythe, a climber who made several attempts on Everest in the 1930s, wrote in a letter that he believed he saw the remains of Mallory and Andrew Irvine through a telescope in 1936. This account, found by Smythe's son Tony while researching his father's life, is the only reported sighting before Conrad Anker found Mallory's body in 1999. The letter, addressed to Edward Norton, leader of the 1924 Everest expedition when Mallory disappeared, described how Smythe scanned the mountain face from base camp. He noticed something unusual in a gully below a scree shelf, at the point where Mallory and Irvine would have fallen. Smythe, whose eyesight was excellent, insisted it was not a rock. The location matched the spot where a previous expedition had found an ice axe believed to be connected to the tragedy. Although Smythe wrote extensively about his expeditions, he omitted the sighting from his published accounts, instructing Norton not to share it publicly to prevent media speculation. The fate of Mallory and Irvine remains one of mountaineering's greatest mysteries, as it is still unknown whether they reached Everest's summit before perishing. Mallory's body was not recovered until 1999. Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first climbers confirmed to reach Everest's summit, with the aid of oxygen, in 1953. Smythe himself reached 28,200 feet in 1933, less than 800 feet from the summit, but was forced to turn back. He made further attempts in subsequent expeditions, including 1936 when he believed he saw Mallory's remains, but never surpassed his previous record.

article_content: A Florida woman claims she scared off an armed robber during her jewelry party by invoking Jesus' name. Jacquie Hagler was hosting 14 female guests at her home when Derek Lee, 24, entered wearing a ski cap and bandana, brandishing a weapon. Lee demanded the guests put their money and phones in his duffel bag, but several guests believed it was a prank or part of the event. One guest pushed Lee’s hand aside, insisting he was only holding a water pistol. Hagler said she felt a sudden boldness, stood up, and declared, 'In the name of Jesus, get out of my house.' Lee responded by threatening to shoot if they didn't comply, but Hagler repeated her command. The guests began chanting, 'Jesus, Jesus, Jesus,' and Lee appeared frightened before fleeing the scene. Donna Bowen, a guest at the party, remarked on the feeling of divine protection, saying, 'You knew that God’s hand was there. It could have gone so differently.' After leaving Hagler’s home, Lee attempted to rob a 62-year-old woman at a nearby Bank of America ATM, but fled when she shouted. Lee was later identified by the party guests and the attempted ATM victim, and was arrested at his father’s nearby home. He was booked into the Columbia County Detention Center on a $200,000 bond for home invasion robbery. Hagler shared that the incident strengthened her faith and that she forgives Lee, praying he will turn his life around.

article_content: American scientists have confirmed the discovery of what is believed to be the world's first known two-headed bull shark fetus. According to a study by Michigan State University, published in the Journal of Fish Biology, the rare specimen was found in the Gulf of Mexico in 2011—about a year after the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. A fisherman discovered the fetus when he opened the uterus of an adult shark. While two-headed sharks have been observed in other species, such as blue sharks and tope sharks, this is the first recorded case in a bull shark (Carcharhinus leucas). Bull sharks are among the few shark species known to sometimes attack humans and are also favored by anglers due to their spirited fights. Michael Wagner, an assistant professor of fisheries and wildlife at Michigan State University, explained that although bull sharks are resilient, the two-headed fetus would likely not have survived long after birth. 'It was near-term, but undersized—the body seems to have invested significant energy in developing a second head, leading to a shortened body,' Wagner noted. MRI scans revealed that the specimen had two distinct heads, hearts, and stomachs, which then merged into a single tail. This rare condition, called polycephaly—and specifically bicephaly or dicephaly for two-headedness—typically results in a short lifespan. Each head has its own brain, and they may struggle to coordinate their movements, sometimes exhibiting disoriented or zig-zagging motions. Such congenital anomalies are more frequently noticed in reptiles like snakes and lizards, often because these are bred in captivity and closely monitored. The bull shark fetus was transferred from Florida Keys Community College to Michigan State University for further examination, where MRI imaging provided more details on its anatomy. Although some speculate that environmental pollution, such as the Deepwater Horizon oil spill, could be linked to such deformities, Wagner emphasized there is no evidence to support any specific cause. According to the International Shark Attack File, there were 80 unprovoked shark attacks on humans in 2012, with seven resulting in fatalities.
translated_content: מדענים אמריקאים אישרו את גילויו של עובר כריש שורי דו-ראשי, שלדעתם זהו המקרה הראשון בעולם שתועד במין זה. על פי מחקר של אוניברסיטת מישיגן סטייט שפורסם ב-Journal of Fish Biology, הדגימה הנדירה נמצאה במפרץ מקסיקו בשנת 2011 — כשנה לאחר דליפת הנפט של Deepwater Horizon. דייג נתקל בעובר כאשר פתח את רחם הכרישה הבוגרת. בעוד שנמצאו כרישים דו-ראשיים במינים אחרים, כמו כריש כחול וכריש טופ, זהו המקרה הראשון שתועד בכריש שורי (Carcharhinus leucas). כרישים שוריים ידועים כאגרסיביים לעיתים כלפי בני אדם ויש להם פופולריות גם בקרב דייגים בזכות הקרב שהם מספקים. מייקל וגנר, פרופסור חבר למדגה וחיות בר באוניברסיטת מישיגן סטייט, הסביר שלמרות שהכרישים השוריים עמידים, העובר הדו-ראשי כנראה לא היה שורד זמן רב לאחר הלידה. "הוא היה קרוב ללידה, אבל קטן מהרגיל – נראה שהגוף השקיע הרבה אנרגיה בפיתוח ראש נוסף, מה שקיצר את שאר הגוף," אמר וגנר. סריקות MRI חשפו שלעובר היו שני ראשים, לבבות וקיבות נפרדים, אשר התאחדו בזנב אחד. מצב נדיר זה נקרא פוליצפליה — ובשני ראשים, בייצפליה או דיסצפליה — ולעיתים קרובות מביא לאורח חיים קצר. כל ראש בעל מוח משלו ולעיתים יש קושי בתיאום תנועות, מה שעלול לגרום לתנועות מעוותות או תזוזה בזיגזג. מומים מולדים כאלה נצפים לעיתים קרובות יותר בזוחלים כמו נחשים ולטאות, לרוב מפני שהם מגודלים בשבי ונמצאים בתצפית רצופה. עובר הכריש הועבר מהמכללה הקהילתית של פלורידה קיז לאוניברסיטת מישיגן סטייט לבדיקות נוספות, שם סיפקו סריקות MRI עוד פרטים על האנטומיה שלו. למרות שיש המשערים שזיהום סביבתי, כמו זה שנגרם מהדליפה של Deepwater Horizon, עשוי להיות קשור למומים האלה, וגנר הדגיש שאין ראיות התומכות בסיבה מסוימת. לפי ארכיון תקיפות הכרישים הבינלאומי, בשנת 2012 התרחשו 80 תקיפות כריש לא מתגרות בבני אדם, שבע מהן היו קטלניות.

article_content: A recent survey conducted by US-based Terror Free Tomorrow indicates that most Iranians are in favor of comprehensive nuclear inspections, democratic governance, and better relations with the United States. The poll shows that a majority believe President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad has not kept his promise of distributing oil profits to the people. The results revealed that 80% of respondents support full nuclear inspections with guarantees not to develop nuclear weapons if Iran receives aid from abroad. While just over half still think possessing nuclear weapons would make the country safer, only 29% rate weapons development as a top priority. When given the option between continuing nuclear arms development or accepting foreign aid, only 17% remained in favor of the weapons program. Improving the economy is the highest priority for respondents, with 88% stating the government should focus on this issue. Additionally, 56% feel Ahmadinejad has failed to deliver on his campaign pledge regarding oil revenue. The poll found that 61% oppose Iran's current system where the Supreme Leader holds unelected religious authority. Instead, 79% support a democratic model with directly elected leaders. Nearly two-thirds of respondents favor supporting groups like Hamas and Hezbollah, yet 55% are in favor of recognizing both Israel and Palestine as independent nations if this would result in normalized relations with the United States. Terror Free Tomorrow conducted telephone interviews in Farsi with 1,000 Iranians, evenly split by gender and covering all 30 provinces of Iran. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus 3 percentage points. The organization explains that telephone interviews were required due to the risk of prosecution for in-person polling, as seen in previous cases where pollsters faced imprisonment. The group's advisory board features US figures such as Senator John McCain, Lee Hamilton, and Tom Kean, and Terror Free Tomorrow participated in the 2006 Clinton Global Initiative.
translated_content: סקר שנערך לאחרונה על ידי הארגון האמריקאי Terror Free Tomorrow מראה כי רוב האיראנים תומכים בפיקוח גרעיני מקיף, בשלטון דמוקרטי ובשיפור היחסים עם ארצות הברית. הסקר מצא כי רוב הנשאלים חושבים שנשיא איראן, מחמוד אחמדינז'אד, לא עמד בהבטחתו לחלק את רווחי הנפט לעם. 80% מהנשאלים תומכים בפיקוח מלא על מתקני הגרעין ובהבטחה לא לפתח נשק גרעיני, בתמורה לסיוע מחו"ל. קצת יותר ממחצית עדיין מאמינים שנשק גרעיני יחזק את ביטחון המדינה, אך רק 29% רואים בפיתוח נשק עדיפות עליונה. כאשר הציגו בפניהם בחירה בין המשך פיתוח נשק גרעיני לבין קבלת סיוע בינלאומי, רק 17% בחרו להישאר בעד תוכנית הנשק. שיפור הכלכלה הוא בראש סדר העדיפויות—88% סבורים שזה צריך להיות היעד העליון של הממשלה. בנוסף, 56% חשים שאחמדינז'אד לא קיים את הבטחתו לגבי רווחי הנפט. הסקר הראה כי 61% מתנגדים לשלטון הנוכחי באיראן, בו המנהיג העליון מחזיק בסמכות דתית ולא נבחר ישירות. במקום זאת, 79% מעדיפים מערכת דמוקרטית המאפשרת בחירות חופשיות וישירות למנהיגות. כמעט שני-שלישים תומכים במתן סיוע לארגונים כמו חמאס וחזבאללה, אך 55% מוכנים להכיר בישראל ובפלסטין כמדינות עצמאיות, אם תהליך זה יביא ליחסים רגילים עם ארה"ב. Terror Free Tomorrow ערך ראיונות טלפוניים בפרסית עם 1,000 איראנים, בחלוקה שווה של גברים ונשים ומכל 30 מחוזות איראן. טעות הדגימה היא פלוס או מינוס 3 אחוזים. הארגון מסביר כי סקרים פנים-אל-פנים מסוכנים באיראן, והיו בעבר מקרים בהם חוקרים נכלאו בעקבות סקרים כאלה. הוועדה המייעצת של הארגון כוללת אישים אמריקאים כגון הסנטור ג'ון מקיין, לי המילטון וטום קין, והארגון השתתף ביוזמת קלינטון הגלובלית ב-2006.

article_content: Every evening under the elevated 7 train in Jackson Heights, Queens, unemployed and often homeless men gather, hungry and in need. Jorge Munoz, a school bus driver by day, arrives around 9:30 p.m. in his white pickup truck stocked with hot food, coffee, and hot chocolate. Since 2004, Munoz estimates he has served more than 70,000 free meals, typically providing chicken and rice to eager recipients. For many, this meal is their only hot food of the day; for some, it is the first food since the previous night. Gratitude fills the air, with regulars like Eduardo expressing thanks for Munoz’s generosity and dedication. For over four years, Munoz and his family have been feeding those in need every night, making the operation a true family effort. Word of Munoz's mobile soup kitchen, now organized as his nonprofit 'An Angel in Queens,' has spread throughout the community. People of diverse backgrounds—Hispanic, Egyptian, Chinese, Ethiopian, South Asian, white and black Americans, and even a British man—all line up for a warm meal. Munoz is motivated by empathy rooted in his own immigrant experience. Born in Colombia, Munoz moved to the United States in the 1980s after his mother found work in Brooklyn. He became a legal resident in 1987 and eventually a citizen, alongside his mother and sister. Munoz never stood on a street corner for work, but he understands the struggles the men he serves face. His meal service began in 2004, initially by distributing leftover food collected from friends and local businesses. The project quickly grew, with his family preparing and packing more meals each night, reaching up to 140 in recent months. The family's home doubles as a storage and prep center, with large freezers and supplies crowding their living space. The operation runs with military-like precision. Munoz rises at 5 a.m. to drive his bus route, checks in with his family during cooking breaks, and upon returning home in the evening, helps pack and deliver meals. Regardless of weather, he or his sister never misses a night. With the recent economic downturn, donations have slowed while demand has risen sharply. The cost, about $400–$450 each week for food and gasoline, is largely covered from Munoz's $700 weekly paycheck and the family's savings. For Munoz, giving back is a calling; he believes, 'I have everything I need, but these guys don’t. If I can give them a meal today, it makes a difference.' Munoz encourages others to get involved by supporting An Angel in Queens.
translated_content: בכל ערב, מתחת לרכבת 7 המוגבהת בג'קסון הייטס, קווינס, מתאספים גברים מובטלים ולעיתים חסרי בית, רעבים ונזקקים. חורחה מוניוז, נהג אוטובוס בית ספר ביום, מגיע בסביבות 21:30 בטנדר הלבן שלו, מלא אוכל חם, קפה ושוקו חם. מאז 2004, מוניוז מעריך שחילק יותר מ-70,000 ארוחות חינם, לרוב עוף ואורז למקבלי האוכל הנרגשים. עבור רבים זו הארוחה החמה היחידה שלהם במשך היום; עבור חלקם, זה האוכל הראשון מאז אתמול בלילה. תחושת תודה ממלאת את האוויר, כאשר קבועים כמו אדוארדו מביעים תודה על הנדיבות והמסירות של מוניוז. יותר מארבע שנים, מוניוז ומשפחתו מאכילים נזקקים בכל לילה, מה שהופך את העשייה למאמץ משפחתי אמיתי. המטבח הנייד של מוניוז, שכיום פועל כעמותה ״מלאך בקווינס״, התפרסם בקהילה. אנשים מרקעים מגוונים – היספנים, מצרים, סינים, אתיופים, דרום-אסייתים, לבנים, שחורים ואפילו בריטי – כולם עומדים בתור לארוחה חמה. המוטיבציה של מוניוז נובעת מאמפתיה לסיפורו האישי של מהגר. נולד בקולומביה והגיע לארה״ב בשנות ה-80, לאחר שאמו מצאה עבודה בברוקלין. הוא קיבל מעמד חוקי ב-1987 ובהמשך אזרחות יחד עם אמו ואחותו. מוניוז מעולם לא עמד בפינת רחוב כדי למצוא עבודה, אך הוא מבין היטב את קשיי האנשים להם הוא עוזר. המיזם החל ב-2004 כשחילק בתחילה שאריות מזון שאסף מחברים ועסקים מקומיים. הפרויקט צמח במהירות, ומשפחתו החלה להכין ולארוז עוד ועוד ארוחות מדי ערב, ובחודשים האחרונים כ-140 ארוחות בלילה. בית המשפחה משמש גם כמחסן ומרכז הכנה, עם מקפיאים ואספקה שממלאים כל פינה. העבודה מתבצעת בדיוק רב: מוניוז קם ב-5 בבוקר לנהוג את האוטובוס, בודק מצב הבישולים בהפסקות, וכששב הביתה עוזר באריזה ואז יוצא לחלק את המנות. לא משנה אם חם או קר, הוא או אחותו תמיד מגיעים. בעקבות המשבר הכלכלי, התרומות קטנו אך מספר מחוסרי הבית גדל. ההוצאות – כ-400–450 דולר לשבוע לאוכל ודלק – מכוסות בעיקר מהשכר השבועי של מוניוז ($700) ומהחסכונות המשפחתיים. עבורו, הנתינה היא שליחות: 'יש לי כל מה שאני צריך, אבל להם אין. אם אוכל לתת להם ארוחה – זה עושה את ההבדל.' מוניוז קורא גם לכם להצטרף ולעזור לעמותת ״מלאך בקווינס״.

article_content: Indian benchmark indices Nifty 50 and Sensex recorded their third straight week of gains, largely driven by robust performance in the information technology sector amid a more favorable global interest rate outlook. This week, the NSE Nifty 50 index advanced 1.58%, registering its strongest week in two months, while the Sensex climbed 1.37%. IT stocks, which generate significant revenue from the US, surged 5.07%, marking their best weekly performance in 16 months. Analysts suggest that after a sharp rise in recent sessions and as the Nifty approaches key resistance levels, the market may enter a phase of short-term consolidation. Jatin Gedia of Sharekhan highlights the support zone at 19,630–19,600 as crucial for the continuation of the uptrend. Similarly, Rupak De from LKP Securities observes a bullish market sentiment, noting that the 'buy on dips' strategy has been favored after Nifty crossed the important 19,500 level. Nifty’s support levels are identified at 19,630 and 19,500, with resistance at 19,850 and 20,000. In the US, Wall Street ended the week on a positive note, extending its rally as encouraging inflation data fueled hopes the Federal Reserve will hold or cut interest rates. The S&P 500 settled at 4,514.02, up 2.2% for the week. The Dow and Nasdaq also posted gains. European shares rose as well, with the STOXX 600 index up 2.8% amid optimism over future rate cuts. Technical indicators such as the MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence) signal a bullish trend for companies like Tata Investment, Indian Railway Finance Corporation, HDFC AMC, Birla Corporation, Rainbow Children's Medicare, and Marico. Conversely, Metro Brands, P&G Health, WABCO India, Castrol India, Nazara Technologies, and Raymond show signs of potential weakness. Among the most active stocks by value on the NSE were SBI, HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance, Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, RIL, and TCS. By trading volume, SBI, Tata Steel, Power Grid, Coal India, Axis Bank, ONGC, and HDFC Bank led the way. Strong buying interest pushed shares of SBI Life, Apollo Hospital, L&T, Hero MotoCorp, Bajaj Auto, Tata Consumer, and Eicher Motors to fresh 52-week highs, signaling a bullish sentiment. In contrast, Rajesh Exports hit a 52-week low, indicating selling pressure. Overall market sentiment was positive, with market breadth favoring bulls: 1,926 stocks closed higher versus 1,813 that ended lower. In other business news: The Indian government is considering the legality of transferring unclaimed funds from the Sahara-Sebi Refund Account to the Consolidated Fund of India, allowing investors to claim refunds later. Apple aims to reach iPhone production worth nearly ₹1 lakh crore in India for FY24. Nawaz Modi, estranged wife of Gautam Singhania, is seeking three-quarters of the industrialist’s net worth for herself and her two daughters as part of the couple’s settlement.

article_content: The Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority (DIEZ) has announced the launch of a $136 million venture capital fund aimed at supporting technology startups. Established under the patronage of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, and in the presence of Sheikh Ahmed bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Second Deputy Ruler of Dubai, the fund is designed to promote the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda (D33) by fostering the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) across emerging sectors.  Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of DIEZ, stated that the establishment of this venture capital fund marks a significant step for successful companies seeking to expand globally. He emphasized that the fund will enhance Dubai’s reputation as a hub for innovative, advanced, and creative enterprises.  According to Dubai Chambers, nearly 30% of Dubai’s startup community comprises Indian entrepreneurs. Indian-owned companies and Non-Resident Indian (NRI) entities have generated over one million jobs in the UAE. As of 2022, almost 83,000 Indian-owned companies were registered with Dubai Chambers.  Dr Mohammed Al Zarooni, Executive Chairman of DIEZ, noted that the fund’s primary goal is to strategically invest in startups demonstrating strong growth potential. He added that the initiative is open to entrepreneurs from around the world and is adaptable to new opportunities and contemporary technologies that align with its objectives.

article_content: Securing cheap housing in Silicon Valley is nearly impossible, but Eric Simons found an unusual workaround. After graduating high school, Simons entered AOL’s Imagine K12 program in Palo Alto to develop his education startup, ClassConnect. He chose not to go to college and moved from Chicago to California to pursue his business. When his initial funding ran out, Simons couldn’t afford rent, so he discreetly lived inside AOL’s offices. He used the gym for showers, ate leftovers and snacks from meetings, and got by with minimal spending. He said he only spent about $30 during this period, aside from a splurge at Thanksgiving. While Simons acknowledges that living in the office wasn’t exactly above board, he felt it was necessary for his company’s survival. Today, ClassConnect operates and is close to landing another $500,000 in funding. AOL acknowledged Simons’ resourcefulness, noting they didn’t expect someone to take entrepreneurship that far. Simons now shares this story with investors, using it as proof of his commitment to success.

Connections is the newest puzzle game from The New York Times. Each day, the game challenges you to sort a set of 16 words into four secret groups by figuring out how the words are related. The puzzle updates every night at midnight and varies in difficulty from day to day. Like Wordle, you can track your winning streak and compare your results with friends. Some puzzles are more challenging than others. If you're stuck on today's Connections puzzle, check out our tips and hints below. If you still can't solve it, we'll reveal the answers at the end.

In Connections, you'll see a grid of 16 words. Your goal is to organize the words into four groups of four by identifying what links them together. The groups might be based on things like video game franchises, book series, shades of red, chain restaurant names, and more. Some words might seem to fit into several themes, but there's only one completely correct solution. You can shuffle and rearrange the words to spot connections more easily. Each group is color-coded: yellow is the easiest, followed by green, blue, then purple, which is the hardest. Pick four words and hit Submit—if you're correct, those words leave the grid and their shared theme is revealed. Incorrect guesses count as mistakes, and you can make up to four before the game ends.

We can help you solve today's Connections by sharing the four themes. Need more help? We'll give you one word from each group below. Still stumped? Don't worry—the puzzle is meant to be tricky. If you just want today's answers, we've got them at the bottom. Connections puzzles change daily, so if you couldn't solve it today, check back tomorrow for a new challenge.

article_content: Abu Dhabi International Airport’s much-anticipated Terminal A is now open, positioning the city as a key player in global tourism, trade, and business. As the UAE’s capital and wealthiest emirate, Abu Dhabi is known for its oil and gas reserves but has been in the shadow of Dubai’s bustling international airport, which achieved $1.7 billion in duty-free sales in 2022. The new Terminal A, just over 80 miles from Dubai, is among the world’s largest airport terminals, significantly expanding the airport’s capacity and intensifying competition with regional hubs. Designed to draw travelers from nearby airports such as Hamad International in Qatar and Sharjah International, Terminal A offers expanded retail and passenger services. The terminal, triple the size of the old main terminal, features a 380,000 square foot shopping and dining area with 163 retail and dining outlets. Passengers can shop at luxury brands like Gucci, Salvatore Ferragamo, Yves Saint Laurent, and Muji—opening its first airport store globally, with items from luggage to health, beauty, and fashion essentials. Lagardère Capital, a joint venture of Lagardère Travel Retail and Abu Dhabi Capital Group, will operate a major segment of the travel retail. Dining includes Jones The Grocer, Taste of India, Starbucks, Camden Food Co., McDonald's, and TGI Fridays. At the high end, chef Todd English is debuting his first airport restaurant, Pub & Market, serving global cuisine—from sushi to gourmet steaks, with runway views. Travelers can access two health and beauty spas in the terminal. Terminal A boasts many biometric touchpoints, such as self-service bag drops, e-gates, and facial recognition at screening, with baggage systems handling up to 19,200 bags per hour for quicker processing. Almost 30 airlines will move to Terminal A by mid-November. Etihad Airways, the UAE’s national carrier, will be the primary tenant, featuring lounges on three levels. Terminal A is central to Etihad’s growth strategy, eventually accommodating up to 45 million passengers yearly. Before opening, Etihad expanded its network through a code-share with Scandinavian Airlines (SAS), adding flights to Dusseldorf, Copenhagen, Osaka, and increasing service to Kuala Lumpur, Colombo, and Nairobi. Etihad serves over 70 routes, but lags behind Qatar Airways (over 160 destinations) and Emirates (144 destinations), especially to the Americas. While Abu Dhabi’s retail revenue is not yet on par with other regional airports, Terminal A may help it attract new travelers. Elena Sorlini, managing director and interim CEO of Abu Dhabi Airports, said Terminal A will help boost Abu Dhabi’s aviation growth and attract more businesses and tourists in the future.

article_content: Superman & Lois will conclude with its fourth season, officially ending The CW’s Arrowverse saga. Fans are looking forward to the last adventures of Clark Kent and Lois Lane. Filming is set to take place from January 11 to April 22, 2024, following resolution of the Hollywood writers’ and actors’ strikes, according to Creative BC (via Richmond News). While the new season’s filming sites haven’t been identified, previous seasons made use of Richmond, Surrey, and Delta in Canada. With production now on schedule, the series is expected to premiere on The CW after filming wraps up, with The Hollywood Reporter emphasizing extra time for complex visual effects, aiming for a high-quality finale. Unlike in past years when episodes aired while filming was underway, Season 4 is a shorter, 10-episode run, with a condensed production timeline. article_content: By Suzannah Hills. The British embassy is temporarily withdrawing some of its staff from Libya as political unrest in the country grows. A statement on the embassy's website said the decision was driven by concerns about Libya's political uncertainty and the risk of clashes between rival armed groups in the capital, Tripoli. 'Given the security implications of ongoing political uncertainty, the British Embassy is temporarily withdrawing a small number of staff,' the statement said, noting that the embassy would continue normal operations. Earlier today, a bomb exploded outside a police station in Benghazi, damaging the building and shattering windows of a nearby school. Vehicles were also damaged in the blast. A British security source told Reuters that only non-essential staff were affected by the embassy's decision. A police official reported that someone threw a bag of explosive material in front of the police station's gate, causing the explosion and significant damage, but no injuries. Around the same time, at about 4 a.m., a second police station in the city was struck by a smaller explosive device, possibly a grenade, according to a witness. No injuries were reported. Police stations in Benghazi have been targeted with explosives at least four times in the past month. Meanwhile, in Tripoli, armed men surrounded the justice ministry on April 30, calling for a purge of officials linked to former ruler Muammar Gaddafi. That same day, protesters demonstrated outside the Libyan General National Congress in support of the Political Isolation Law, which demands the expulsion of former regime employees from political positions.

article_content: A man suspected of committing an armed robbery was apprehended near London Bridge on Thursday afternoon, after courageous bystanders subdued him when he fled through a bustling pub carrying what appeared to be an AK47-like rifle. The event unfolded just before 2pm on Borough High Street, in the wake of an attempted robbery at a nearby Barclays bank branch. Customers at The George pub, situated close to the bank, took shelter when the suspect entered with the weapon. Several individuals tackled and detained him until armed officers arrived and arrested a man in his 30s, described as black and dressed in a blue T-shirt, near Guy’s Hospital. According to the Metropolitan Police, the suspect was detained by the public before police got there. Officers reported that no one was injured and no shots were fired. A weapon was recovered, and authorities stated they are not looking for further suspects. Eyewitnesses documented the unfolding scene on social media. ITV’s deputy news editor Darren Burn, present at The George, observed the suspect carrying what looked like an assault rifle and a Sports Direct bag. Another witness, Ian Macfarlaine, tweeted about the suspect waving a gun inside the pub, while Mike Finnerty described patrons diving for cover. The George, a well-liked pub among both tourists and local workers, was especially crowded due to the warm weather. The Tower Bridge Flying Squad is heading the investigation. Police confirmed that the suspect is being held at a south London police station.
